question.problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{n}^{4}(3x-3)^{n}=(3x-3)+{2}^{4}(3x-3)^{2}+{3}^{4}(3x-3)^{3}+⋯\,.
$$

$R=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}={n}^{4}(3x-3)^{n}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(n+1)^{4}(3x-3)^{n+1}}{{n}^{4}(3x-3)^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(n+1)^{4}(3x-3)}{{n}^{4}}| \\  & =|3x-3|{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{n+1}{n})}^{4} \\  & =|3x-3|\cdot 1 \\  & =3|x-1|\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied if $|x-1|<\frac{1}{3}.$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\frac{1}{3}.$
